subject: AI & Agents
title: AI Agents: The Next Frontier
description: Learn AI Agents: The Next Frontier in one minute.

hook.text: What if AI didn't just answer questions but actually completed tasks for you?

buildup.text: AI agents combine language models with tools — browsers, code interpreters, APIs.

discovery.text: They break complex goals into steps, execute them, and adjust based on results.

twist.text: Early agents sometimes went rogue — booking wrong flights, deleting files, spending money.

climax.text: The race is on to make agents reliable enough to trust with real-world tasks.

punchline.text: From answering to acting — AI's next leap.

quiz.question: What makes AI agents different from chatbots?
options: They can take actions and use external tools

details.summary: AI agents represent the next evolution: systems that plan, use tools, browse the web, write code, and take autonomous action. They move AI from answering questions to completing complex real-world tasks.
details.whyItMatters: Agents transform AI from a question-answering tool into an autonomous worker. This shift creates enormous productivity potential but also introduces new safety and control challenges.
takeaways: AI agents autonomously plan and execute multi-step tasks
They can use tools, browse the web, and write code
Agency introduces new challenges for safety and oversight

faq.question: What makes AI agents different from chatbots?
faq.answer: Chatbots respond to prompts with text. Agents break tasks into steps, select tools, take actions, observe results, and adapt their approach — much more like a human assistant completing a project.

faq.question: What are the biggest risks with AI agents?
faq.answer: Agents that act autonomously can make irreversible mistakes, be exploited through prompt injection, or pursue goals in harmful ways. Maintaining human oversight while enabling autonomous action is the core challenge.
